criterion_notes.c1: No. The study examines multi-level water-resources governance of an inter-basin bulk raw-water transfer project (Projeto de Integração do Rio São Francisco - PISF) under Brazil's National Water Resources Policy (Lei n. 9.433/1997), which delivers raw water to strategic state reservoirs rather than household or community water supply or sanitation service access (Exclusion Criterion 7). Downstream municipal water supply systems are noted only as unmaintained secondary physical infrastructure outside the transposition axes.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording of Criterion 2: YES — the study explicitly analyzes legal, institutional, and governance arrangements (Lei n. 9.433/1997, SGIB under Decreto n. 5.995/2006, CBHSF/CNRH, Codevasf, and Ostrom's IAD rules-in-use). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2: NO — the paper examines macro-level river-basin and inter-basin bulk water governance (voting blocs and centralization in SGIB, civil society representation in CBHSF/CNRH, interagency fragmentation, and state vs. indigenous ontologies of water), with only brief descriptive mentions of bulk O&M charges to states/authorized canal pumpers and weak canal monitoring on private properties, rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access. Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the overall study decision remains exclude (plain_criterion2_decision = exclude) because it fails C1 and C4 as a water-resources governance study without evaluated household/community service-access outcomes.
criterion_notes.c3: Yes. Qualitative empirical case study combining documentary analysis (EIA, legislation, CGU/TCU audit reports) and primary open-ended interviews conducted between 2015 and 2018 with federal/state officials (MI, APAC, Compesa, Codevasf), researchers/civil society (Fundaj, OGA), one quilombola community in Garanhuns, and two indigenous communities in Ibimirim and Pesqueira, analyzed in NVivo 11.
criterion_notes.c4: No. Empirically analyzed outcomes are macro-governance and socio-environmental outcomes: power and information asymmetries in SGIB and CBHSF, interagency fragmentation, silencing of indigenous (Pipipã) and quilombola voices in river-basin governance, and destruction of 1,250 km² of native Caatinga. General contextual remarks about supply collapses in Semiárido towns due to obsolete secondary supply infrastructure and unequal water distribution across localities are not empirically evaluated household/community service-access outcomes of a legal/administrative rule.
criterion_notes.c5: Yes for its own institutional water-resources research design: unit of analysis (PISF institutional action arena), governance arrangements, institutional/participatory outcomes, and qualitative case-study methodology are identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Yes. Full text is in Portuguese, which is eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: A governança da água PISF, analisada sob ótica de análise do IAD, refere-se à arena de ação. O PISF constitui um empreendimento de infraestrutura hídrica composto por dois sistemas independentes — os eixos Norte e Leste — que captam as águas do rio São Francisco entre as barragens de Sobradinho e Itaparica, em Pernambuco.

Dessa forma, a transposição conduz volumes adequados de água para os reservatórios estratégicos estaduais, sendo distribuída para as demais estruturas de abastecimento hídrico. No entanto, a ausência de manutenção dessas estruturas secundárias compromete os investimentos no projeto, uma vez que os eixos da transposição dependem da infraestrutura existente para garantir a chegada das águas aos consumidores finais.

A subordinação do CBHSF ao CNRH limita a governança participativa, reduz a representação da sociedade civil nos comitês e dificulta a cooperação interescala e a resolução de conflitos. As regras de limite e fiscalização do acesso às águas transpostas são frágeis (canais em propriedades privadas e usos difusos); a sustentabilidade financeira depende de tarifas e de uma oferta raramente excedente, abrindo espaço para conflitos

Este estudo adota uma abordagem metodológica de natureza qualitativa (Godoi & Balsini, 2010), e a coleta de dados foi realizada entre os anos de 2015 e 2018, conforme a realização de entrevistas em formato conversacional, livre e padronizado aberto, com o objetivo de compreender os significados atribuídos aos problemas da governança da água (Creswell, 2010).

Em relação à arena de ação, os atores estatais detêm papel central, mas há assimetria de poder e de informação em relação às organizações locais, comunidades indígenas e quilombolas, e associações civis. A participação é prevista formalmente, porém, na prática, prevalece a centralização decisória da União e estados.

raw_response.exposure: Multi-level water-resources governance arrangements of the PISF inter-basin bulk water transfer under Lei n. 9.433/1997 (SGIB decision-making structure, CBHSF/CNRH representation, Codevasf/state agency coordination, and Ostrom IAD rules-in-use)
raw_response.outcome: Institutional water-governance and socio-environmental outcomes: federal/state decision-making centralization, power and information asymmetries in SGIB and CBHSF, interagency fragmentation, marginalization of indigenous (Pipipã) and quilombola voices, and loss of 1,250 km² of native Caatinga vegetation
raw_response.population_and_sample: Institutional action arena of the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF) in Pernambuco and Northeast Brazil; qualitative interviews (2015–2018) with federal/state agency representatives (MI, APAC, Compesa, Codevasf), researchers/civil society (Fundaj, OGA), 1 quilombola community in Garanhuns, and 2 indigenous communities in Ibimirim and Pesqueira
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic — water-resources governance study unrelated to household or community service access, per Exclusion Criterion 7; also fails Criterion 2 narrow rule-type scope and Criterion 4 service-access outcome). Using Ostrom's IAD framework, this qualitative study examines multi-level river-basin and inter-basin bulk raw-water governance in the São Francisco River Integration Project (PISF) under Brazil's National Water Resources Policy (Lei n. 9.433/1997). Its analysis centers on intergovernmental centralization in SGIB, limited civil-society influence in CBHSF/CNRH, interagency fragmentation, ontological conflicts with indigenous (Pipipã) and quilombola communities, and Caatinga deforestation. It does not examine a rule-type legal/administrative mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access, nor does it empirically evaluate household/community service-access outcomes (noting only in passing that downstream municipal supply infrastructure outside the bulk transfer canals is physically obsolete). Even under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, the study remains excluded for failing C1 and C4.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative institutional case study (documentary analysis and open-ended interviews analyzed with Ostrom's IAD framework in NVivo 11)
